regional.syndrome: About 80% of infections are asymptomatic; 20% develop West Nile fever; <1% develop neuroinvasive disease — meningitis, encephalitis or a poliomyelitis-like acute flaccid paralysis, with substantial mortality and long-term sequelae in older adults.
regional.headline: Globally the most widespread encephalitic flavivirus, maintained in a bird–mosquito cycle.
regional.prevention: Mosquito control and personal protection; blood-supply nucleic-acid screening; equine vaccines exist but no human vaccine.
regional.geography: Africa, Europe, Middle East, Asia, Australia (Kunjin), and across the Americas since 1999.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Sindbis virus. Pogosta/Ockelbo disease: fever, rash and arthralgia.
regional.geography: Sindbis virus. Pogosta/Ockelbo disease: fever, rash and arthralgia.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: In animals: encephalitis, ataxia and abortion. In humans: antibodies reported in febrile patients and veterinary workers in Nigeria and South Africa; one historical isolation from a febrile child is cited in older literature, but a defined human syndrome is not established.
regional.headline: Simbu-serogroup virus causing neurological disease in horses and ruminants in southern Africa, with serological and occupational evidence pointing to human exposure.
regional.prevention: Vector avoidance; occupational precautions in veterinary work.
regional.geography: Sub-Saharan Africa (notably South Africa, Nigeria), with detections in Israel.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
